Kuvitus: suuren hiukkasilmaisimen pääty: Illustration: the end of a large particle detector seen from the front. The detector is an octagonal, many-layered structure with a thin beam pipe through its centre. In the middle two protons have collided, and curved particle tracks fly out in every direction from the collision point as orange, blue, green and red lines. A person stands on the floor next to the detector, only a small fraction of its height.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kolme suure: Schematic figure, not to scale: three magnifications from left to right. On the left an atom, about 10 to the power minus 10 metres: a light blue electron cloud with three blue electrons and a small nucleus in the middle. In the middle the nucleus magnified, about 10 to the power minus 14 metres: red protons and grey neutrons packed tightly together. On the right one proton magnified, about 10 to the power minus 15 metres: inside it three quarks u, u and d with spring-like lines of gluons between them. Quarks and electrons are smaller than about 10 to the power minus 18 metres.
Standardimallin perushiukkaset taulukkon: The elementary particles of the Standard Model as a table. The first three columns are generations I, II and III. The top two rows hold the quarks: u, c and t, charge plus two thirds e, and d, s and b, charge minus one third e. The bottom two rows hold the leptons: the electron, muon and tau, charge minus e, and their neutrinos, charge zero. The fourth column holds the mediator particles: the gluon, photon and Z boson, charge zero, and the W bosons, charge plus or minus e. The fifth column holds the Higgs boson H, charge zero. The quarks are in sand-coloured, the leptons in light blue, the mediators in green and the Higgs boson in reddish boxes.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: vasemmalla: Schematic figure, not to scale: on the left a proton, a circle with a red outline containing two u quarks and one d quark joined by spring-like lines of gluons. Below it: the proton p is uud, and its charge is plus two thirds plus two thirds minus one third, that is plus 1 elementary charge. On the right a neutron, a circle with a grey outline containing one u quark and two d quarks. Below it: the neutron n is udd, and its charge is plus two thirds minus one third minus one third, that is 0.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa, kaksi tapah: Schematic figure, not to scale, two events. On the left annihilation: at the top a blue electron and a red positron move towards each other, blue velocity arrows. Lower down they have disappeared, and two orange photons leave the meeting point in opposite directions, each with an energy of 511 kiloelectronvolts. On the right pair production: an orange photon whose energy hf is at least 1.022 megaelectronvolts comes close to an atomic nucleus and turns into an electron and a positron, which leave in different directions.
Kaavakuva sähkömagneettisesta vuorovaiku: Schematic figure of the electromagnetic interaction, time runs from bottom to top. Two electrons approach each other from below. At the point where they are closest, an orange wavy line, the exchanged photon gamma, passes between them. After that the electrons move apart: they repel each other. At the left edge an arrow pointing upwards, time.
Kaavakuva beeta miinus -hajoamisesta kva: Schematic figure of beta minus decay at the quark level, time runs from left to right. On the left a neutron n, quarks u, d and d. Three horizontal lines run to the right. The top two quarks, u and d, continue unchanged. The d quark on the bottom line turns into a u quark in the middle and emits a purple wavy line, a W minus boson, which travels down and to the right and turns into an electron e minus and an electron antineutrino. On the right a proton p, quarks u, d and u.
